examples.en: Please mark the wrong problems with a cross.
The teacher put a cross on the wrong answer.
If it's right, make a circle. If it's wrong, make a cross.
Don't put a cross in this box.
There are so many crosses on my test paper that I'm upset.
A cross mark is also called an X mark.

explain: 동그라미(○)와 반대로 틀렸다는 표시를 말해요. '가위표를 하다/치다'처럼 써요. 같은 모양을 '엑스(X) 표시'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I marked the wrong answer with an X.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치다'는 줄이나 표시를 그을 때 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 치다 is the verb used for drawing a line or a mark.

phrases.en: I put an X mark on the wrong question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가위표'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 가위표 and common in speech.

phrases.en: If it's right, I draw a circle, and if it's wrong, an X.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞음과 틀림을 나란히 말할 때 두 낱말을 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two words are used together to talk about right and wrong.

explain_en: It is the opposite of a circle (○) and shows that an answer is wrong. You say '가위표를 하다/치다'. The same mark is also called an 'X 표시'.

examples.en: Our club is recruiting new members.
The company recruited new employees.
I saw a notice recruiting volunteers.
Until when do you plan to recruit participants?
I'll let you know as soon as we recruit students.
I was surprised that more people signed up than expected.

explain: 사람을 구하는 쪽이 '모집하다'를 쓰고, 들어가려는 쪽은 '지원하다'를 써요. 회사가 최종으로 뽑아서 일을 시키는 건 '채용하다'예요. 광고에는 '신입 사원 모집'처럼 '하다' 없이 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: Our store is recruiting part-time workers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모집하다'의 해요체로, 사람을 구하는 쪽이 현재의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form of 모집하다, used by the side that is looking for people.

phrases.en: We are recruiting new members right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중'을 붙여 지금 모집이 진행되고 있다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 중 shows that recruiting is going on right now.

phrases.example: 이번 달에는 신입 사원을 모집하지 않아요.
phrases.en: We are not recruiting new employees this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 지금은 사람을 구하지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say you are not looking for people now.

explain_en: The side looking for people uses 모집하다, and the side wanting to join uses '지원하다' (apply). When a company finally selects someone and hires them, that is '채용하다'. Ads drop 하다 and just say '신입 사원 모집'.

en: to return (a borrowed item); to give back

examples.ko: 저는 일주일에 한 번 도서관에 책을 반납해요.
examples.en: I return books to the library once a week.
I returned the umbrella I borrowed yesterday to my friend.
By when do I have to return this book?
If you return it late, you have to pay.
I returned the hotel key and left.

examples.ko: 반납하러 갔는데 도서관 문이 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I went to return it, but the library was closed.

explain: 책, 열쇠, 우산, 렌터카처럼 '빌린 것'을 돌려줄 때 써요. 산 물건을 가게에 돌려주고 돈을 받는 건 '환불하다'예요. 빌린 돈을 돌려줄 때는 '반납하다'가 아니라 '갚다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 책을 다 읽으면 도서관에 반납해 주세요.
phrases.en: When you finish the book, please return it to the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌려 간 사람에게 돌려 달라고 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to give back what they borrowed.

phrases.en: Today is the day to return the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 날'을 붙여 돌려줘야 하는 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -는 날 to refer to the day something must be returned.

phrases.en: I'm sorry I returned the book late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늦게'를 앞에 붙여 정해진 때보다 늦은 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 늦게 means returning after the due time.

explain_en: Use it for things you borrowed: books, keys, umbrellas, rental cars. Taking a purchase back to a shop for your money is '환불하다'. For borrowed money, use '갚다', not '반납하다'.

examples.en: I set up the chairs in advance before a meeting.
Yesterday I set up my new computer.
We will set up the stage tomorrow morning.

examples.ko: 머리를 세팅하는 데 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes to style my hair.
I set the seats and waited for the guests.
I set the alarm and woke up early.

explain: 컴퓨터 준비, 행사장 준비, 머리 모양 만들기에 모두 써요. 영어 setting에서 온 외래어라서 대화에서 많이 들리고, 글에서는 '준비하다'나 '설정하다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 손님이 오기 전에 상을 세팅해 놓았어요.
phrases.en: I set the table before the guests came.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of preparing in advance.

phrases.en: I set the alarm on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 앱의 기능을 맞출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adjusting a device or app function.

explain_en: It covers setting up a computer, preparing an event space, and styling hair. It is a loanword from English 'setting', common in speech; in writing '준비하다' or '설정하다' often sounds more natural.

en: to write; to fill in; to draw up

examples.ko: 이 서류를 오늘 안에 작성해 주세요.
examples.en: Please fill out this form by the end of today.
I wrote my résumé last night.

examples.ko: 보고서를 작성하는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to write a report.
Write your name and address in this box.
I wrote the email and sent it right away.

examples.ko: 계획서를 작성할 때는 이 예시를 참고하세요.
examples.en: Use this example as a reference when you write the plan.

explain: 일기나 편지처럼 마음 가는 대로 쓰는 글은 '쓰다'이고, '작성하다'는 서류·보고서·이력서처럼 형식이 있는 문서에 어울려요. 은행이나 병원에서 종이를 주며 '작성해 주세요'라고 자주 말해요. 일상 대화에서 '일기를 작성했어요'라고 하면 조금 딱딱하게 들려요.

phrases.en: I fill out an application form at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, '쓰다' is used more than '작성하다'.

phrases.en: Please tell me how to write a résumé.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 쓰는 방식을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking how to write a document.

phrases.en: Please hand in the document you filled out at the counter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 다 쓴 문서를 앞에서 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a document that has already been written.

explain_en: For diaries or letters you simply say '쓰다'. 작성하다 suits documents with a set format, such as forms, reports and résumés. At a bank or hospital you will often hear '작성해 주세요' when they hand you a form. Saying '일기를 작성했어요' (a diary) in conversation would sound stiff.

p.n: Works, but the replacement is plainer and less formal.
